name: Slate Edge
effective_cost: Free, with no annual fee, but no rewards program and a high ongoing APR
balance_transfer_fee: Either $5 or 5% of the amount of each transfer, whichever is greater
penalty_apr_trigger: Failing to make a Minimum Payment when due, or making a payment that's returned unpaid; can remain in effect indefinitely
pay_over_time_fee: Up to 1.72% per month of the amount selected to pay over time, via Chase Pay Over Time

verdict.text: No rewards and a high APR; Freedom Rise is the better no-fee starter card

earn_note: Slate Edge has no cash back or points program of any kind. Chase's official page now shows a flat ~29% variable APR with no 0% intro period, a change from the intro-APR/rate-reduction mechanic this card originally launched with. If you want cash back on a no-fee, no-credit-history-required Chase starter card, use Freedom Rise instead.

points.note: This card has no points or cash-back program of any kind. Chase's official page shows a flat ~29% variable APR and no longer mentions any 0% intro period or the ongoing APR-reduction mechanic this card launched with in 2021.

transfer_partners.highlight: No rewards currency exists on this card, so there is nothing to transfer.

credits.name: DoorDash DashPass
credits.subtitle: 6 mo free, then $10/quarter promo
credits.description: 6 months of complimentary DashPass membership ($0 delivery fees on DoorDash/Caviar). Separately, up to $10/quarter in statement credits on non-restaurant (grocery/retail) DoorDash orders through Dec 2027.
tips: Cancel DashPass before the 6-month free trial ends if you don't want to start paying for it.
The $10/quarter non-restaurant credit is the only ongoing recurring value here.

insurance.detail: +1 year (on warranties ≤3 years, up to 4 years total)

protection_note: Modest, as expected for a starter card: purchase protection, extended warranty, and secondary rental car coverage exist, but no trip cancellation, baggage, or cell phone coverage.
rental_note: Secondary coverage only: it pays after your personal auto insurance, covering what's left. Use a card with primary coverage for rentals when possible.

services.name: Automatic credit line reviews
services.detail: Chase automatically checks the account for a credit line increase every 6 months or sooner.

services.name: Roadside assistance
services.detail: Dispatch service for roadside emergencies; fees billed to your card at time of dispatch.

services.name: Foreign transaction fee likely applies
services.detail: Not listed among Chase's no-foreign-transaction-fee cards; treat it as carrying the standard fee abroad.

additional_cards.title: Additional cards
additional_cards.note: No distinct authorized-user program is marketed for this card.

timeline.text: As of this check, Chase's official page shows a flat ~29% variable APR with no 0% intro period and no mention of the automatic APR-reduction mechanic the card launched with. The card remains open to new applicants, contrary to this dataset's earlier discontinued status.

Chase introduces Slate Edge as a no-annual-fee card built around an interest rate that could go down over time with responsible use, rather than around rewards. Launched with a 12-month 0% intro APR and a $100 statement credit for spending $500 in the first 6 months.
